concepts.label: Glare Kill
concepts.angle: Open on the exact moment screen glare disappears, then reveal the lamp that did it.
concepts.insight: Desk workers blame their eyes and their monitor, not their lighting, so they never fix the real cause.
concepts.firstFrame: Tight crop of a glaring monitor; a wipe of clean light sweeps the reflection off the screen.
concepts.motionIdea: A light wipe travels across a screenshot, erasing the glare layer to expose crisp text underneath.
concepts.signatureMoment: The Focus Lamp's beam physically peels the glare layer off the monitor like a sticker, revealing the user's actual spreadsheet underneath.
concepts.proof: synthetic demo claim: glare-reducing desk light
concepts.risk: Keep the glare-reduction claim framed as a demo, not a measured result.

concepts.label: Same Desk, Two Lights
concepts.angle: Hold one desk in frame and snap between harsh light and the lamp's tuned light.
concepts.insight: People accept a bad desk setup because they have never seen the same desk look calm.
concepts.firstFrame: A split desk: left half harsh and reflective, right half evenly lit, divider sitting on screen.
concepts.motionIdea: A vertical divider slides across the same desk shot, swapping harsh light for tuned light on a beat.
concepts.signatureMoment: The same desk splits in two and the harsh half crumples away as the Focus Lamp's pool of light shoves the divider off-screen.
concepts.proof: synthetic demo claim: glare-reducing desk light
concepts.risk: Before/after must use the same staged desk so the comparison is honest.

concepts.label: One-Tap Ritual
concepts.angle: POV of a hand starting a focus session with a single tap that tunes the whole desk.
concepts.insight: Starting deep work feels like friction; a one-tap light cue makes the start feel effortless.
concepts.firstFrame: Top-down POV of a hand reaching for the lamp dial as the desk sits in flat, dull light.
concepts.motionIdea: On the tap, light blooms from the lamp and the desk eases from cold flat tone into a warm focused pool.
concepts.signatureMoment: One tap on the Focus Lamp dial and the glare reflections on the screen get pushed past the monitor's edge by the advancing rim of its light pool.
concepts.proof: synthetic demo claim: glare-reducing desk light
concepts.risk: Keep it product-forward; the lamp must stay visible inside the POV.

selectionNote: Glare Kill has the strongest first-2-seconds interrupt and a distinct cold-open-payoff arc; Same Desk is the runner-up and its split-compare beat can graft into the cause-reveal.
